transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because my body just feels completely drained. It's like... I don't know, even walking from my car into the clinic today, or just opening the EHR at work, it takes everything I have. I'm just exhausted.
How long have you been feeling this level of exhaustion?

It's been about nine months. Yeah, around nine months. It basically started right after I crashed from this... this really high-energy period I had. Ever since that ended, I've just been stuck with this depressed, guilty, and completely exhausted feeling.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before this period of exhaustion started?

No, not really. Um... I guess I just haven't really noticed. I'm just so tired all the time that I haven't even tried doing the stuff I used to like. I mostly just go to work and come home, so I'm not really sure.
You mentioned feeling guilty - can you tell me more about that?

Yeah, it's... mostly about work. I just keep replaying every chart and every set of vitals I take in my head. I get this awful feeling like I've somehow hurt the patients. My supervisors keep telling me that nothing bad happened and I didn't do anything wrong, but... I just can't stop feeling like I did.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't. Um... even with how exhausted and bad I feel all the time, I don't want to do anything like that. I haven't had any thoughts about hurting myself.
Have you noticed any changes in your movement or activity level, such as feeling restless or slowed down?

Yeah, definitely slowed down. Um... people at work actually told me I looked slowed down lately. I could feel it, too. It's like... even just doing basic things, like putting a blood pressure cuff away or just answering a simple question, it took me way longer than normal.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past nine months?

Yeah, I did. Um... I just barely wanted food at all. I would end up skipping lunch and dinner most days. I didn't really think about it until I realized my scrubs were hanging a lot looser on me, mostly because I was just drinking coffee or water instead of eating.
Have you experienced any periods where your depression seemed to worsen or improve slightly over the past nine months?
No, not really. It's just been... consistently bad. I haven't noticed any times where it felt like it was getting better or worse, it's just been this heavy, exhausting feeling the whole time.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that would normally bring you happiness?

I don't think so, no. Um... I haven't really noticed a change like that. I guess I still get some enjoyment out of the things I normally like, it's just... like I said, I'm mostly just dealing with that exhausting feeling all the time. But I wouldn't say I can't feel happy about stuff.
Do you often feel worthless?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's mostly about work. I keep replaying every chart I've done, every set of vitals I've taken, just over and over in my head. I get this overwhelming feeling that I've messed up and hurt the patients. Even when my supervisors pull me aside and tell me everything is fine and nothing bad happened, I just... I still feel like I've done something terrible.
Have you experienced any other periods like this in your life before the past nine months?
No, I don't think so. This is... this is the first time it's been like this. I haven't really felt this way before.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety at any point over the past nine months?
No, not really. I mean, I'm exhausted all the time, so I mostly just want to rest. I haven't noticed feeling restless or like I need to move around a lot. I'm just too tired for that.
Would you say that your depression is moderately severe or severe?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I don't know the exact difference between moderately severe and severe, to be honest. I just know it feels really heavy and it's hard to get through the day right now. But I don't know which word fits it better.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest in activities you used to enjoy?
Not really, no. I still care about the stuff I usually like. I mean... I still want to do things, and I still like my hobbies and everything. So, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in them.
Do you think you would enjoy doing your hobbies if you had the energy for them?
Yeah, I think so. If I wasn't so tired all the time, I'd definitely still be doing them. The interest is there, just... not the energy.
Would you say that your lack of participation in hobbies is more because of your tiredness or because you've lost interest in them?

It's definitely the tiredness. My body just feels completely drained right now. Like... even just walking from my car to the clinic today took everything I had. Or at work, just sitting there and opening the EHR takes all my energy. So yeah, it's not that I don't care, I just literally don't have the energy left to do anything extra.
How much weight would you say you've lost over the past nine months?

I don't know the exact number of pounds, honestly. But... I barely wanted food for a while. I would just skip lunch and dinner entirely. I didn't really notice until I realized my scrubs were hanging a lot looser on me at work. I was mostly just drinking coffee or water instead of actually eating. So... a decent amount, I guess, even if I haven't stepped on a scale.
Would you say that if you weren't feeling so tired, your interest in the things you usually enjoy would be about the same as it was before you started feeling this way?
Yeah, I think so. If the exhaustion wasn't there... I'm pretty sure I'd still want to do all the same stuff. I just can't right now.
Can you describe how often your feelings of worthlessness and guilt about work affect your daily life?

It happens pretty much every day. I just... I keep replaying every chart and every set of vitals in my head. I constantly feel like I hurt the patients somehow. And it doesn't even help when my supervisors tell me nothing bad happened. They say everything is fine and I did my job, but I still just feel this awful guilt, like I messed up and caused harm. It really just doesn't stop.
Would you say that your feelings of depression and exhaustion are interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life most of the time?

Yeah, definitely. It... it actually got to the point where I couldn't finish my documentation safely, or even stay focused on my patient-support tasks. Employee health ended up pulling me from work because of it, and they sent me for an emergency evaluation. 

It's affecting my life outside of work, too. Like, I was preparing for my CNA certification, but I had to stop studying for it because I just... I couldn't keep up with it anymore. So yeah, it's interfering with pretty much everything.
